RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

A panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of bias. Academic hiring decisions hinge heavily on departmental fit, interview performance, teaching evaluations, and specific curriculum needs—such as the selected candidate's industry experience—rather than publication counts alone.

Accusing a committee of gender bias without concrete evidence (such as discriminatory remarks or demonstrable procedural violations) will almost certainly damage your professional reputation and future job prospects. Furthermore, a two-week delay for feedback is standard in university bureaucracies. 

Instead of questioning the panel's demographics, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on how to strengthen future applications. Focus on actionable insights regarding your interview and teaching presentation.
